item.title: Applying for a Project Grant
item.description: Follow a residents’ group as it seeks a grant from the fictional Willow Lane Local Projects Scheme to run evening cycling skills sessions for adults. Learn to read the rules, prepare a proposal and report on the project.

children.definition: An expense that the grant rules allow the recipient to pay for with grant funds.
children.example: Under the Willow Lane scheme, hiring helmets for the cycling sessions is an allowable cost.
children.translation_uz: grant hisobidan qoplanishi mumkin boʻlgan xarajat

children.definition: The published start and end days for sending in a request to join a programme or receive financial help.
children.example: The application dates for the Willow Lane scheme are 3 to 21 June, so the cycling group plans to send in its form on 18 June.

children.definition: A public invitation to submit project ideas for consideration by an organisation that can pay for them.
children.example: The Willow Lane scheme issued a call for proposals from local groups that want to help adults become more active.
collocations: respond to a call for proposals

children.definition: Money from another source that covers part of a project's costs alongside the main grant.
children.example: The cycling group named a local association as a possible source of co-financing for instructor fees.
children.translation_uz: loyiha xarajatlarini qoplash uchun grantga qoʻshimcha ravishda boshqa manbadan ajratiladigan mablagʻ

children.definition: A file or document that must be sent with an application for it to be complete.
children.example: For the cycling project, written permission to use the practice area is a required attachment.

children.definition: An important point in a piece of planned work, reached when a key task or stage is complete.
children.example: The team listed completion of the first four evening sessions as a project milestone.
children.translation_uz: loyihadagi muhim vazifa yoki bosqichning yakunlanishi

children.definition: A sum of money that an organisation has officially approved for a particular project or purpose.
children.example: The cycling group received a grant award of £1,200 to pay for instructor fees and helmet hire.

children.definition: The highest amount a programme can approve for one project.
children.example: The cycling group checked the grant ceiling before deciding how much to request for the evening sessions.

children.definition: The standards used to compare submissions and decide which ones to choose.
children.example: One of the selection criteria was local benefit, so the cycling group explained how the sessions would help adults who lacked confidence on a bike.

children.definition: A list showing how the total cost is divided among individual items or categories.
children.example: The cycling group included a cost breakdown showing separate amounts for instructor fees, helmet hire and practice area hire.

children.definition: The rules that determine who is allowed to submit a request for financial help or take part in a programme.
children.example: Under the Willow Lane scheme's eligibility requirements, a group had to be based in the district before it could submit a proposal.

children.definition: A document submitted after a project ends that explains what was done, what was achieved and how the money was used.
children.example: In its completion report, the cycling group would list the sessions it ran, summarise what participants learned and explain how it used the grant.

children.definition: A contribution to a project made by providing goods, services or time free of charge.
children.example: The cycling group listed the free use of six bicycles from a local club as an in-kind contribution.
children.translation_uz: loyihaga buyum, xizmat yoki mehnat shaklida qoʻshilgan hissa

children.definition: A description of how and when a team will gather and use information to judge whether its project achieved its goals.
children.example: The cycling group's evaluation plan called for riders to rate their confidence before the first session and after the last.
